dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the briefing book and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The council calendar review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can deliver a two-minute press update without strain.
That is brief and scripted.
It does not use the same voice as moderating a rehearsal.
Someone new shadowed me in the press office this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the budget sessions into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
On 4 March, I held one 60-minute budget-message rehearsal after the team annotated the Q-and-A grid.
How did you do at the next morning's council press conference?
I spoke clearly through the entire question period.
I prepare spokespeople with a written Q-and-A grid and recorded sample answers.
Can they rehearse from those alone first?
Yes, they can flag only the answers that need live work.
I archived last cycle's notes on the council calendar and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
You gave a long welcome at the volunteer awards night.
That was amplified, and there was no 08:30 council conference the next day.
It was not an equivalent demand.
A vendor call about the briefing book ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the press office checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the budget sessions.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the council calendar records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
On 21 April, I moderated two evening rehearsal panels before the 08:30 transit-budget press conference.
What went wrong?
My voice became thin during the opening statement and the deputy read the final responses.
I sketched next week's plan for the budget sessions before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the briefing book updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
I have a recurring migraine pattern after late screen-and-speech sessions, and my physician has emphasized sleep regularity during recovery.
Could the Q-and-A grid reduce the late work?
Yes, it lets us reserve a brief live check for the difficult questions.
The chief of staff says the two-panel rehearsal would impress council members who attend.
Does that change tomorrow's press conference?
No, reporters are already confirmed for 08:30.
I closed the week by updating the press office handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Before Friday's 08:30 transit-budget press conference, should I rank two Thursday evening rehearsal panels above the written Q-and-A review and one live check?
